imagined: Hayley shuts the laptop around 17:00. She half-finishes a Teams thread, puts the heating on or argues with herself about it, and maybe rings her sister while the crumble bakes.

Junior is on a free Friday before two 07:00 starts. He might have a can or two, would probably have football or a podcast on the radio, and at some point his mood would dip over something small (no clean pans, his knees, a late bus that morning) before he cheers up again.

Yousif turns up wanting to cook his rice and lamb, finds the hob taken and the counter covered, and gets curt. He takes stew partly because money is tight, then goes back to his room fairly quickly. The dishes or the noise might cause a small cold moment.
The heating bill is a worry all three share. In mid-November that gets at least one exchange ('can we put it on for an hour?'), especially with Hayley's asthma and the cold damp.
Repetition would be natural, not word-for-word. People don't ask the same person 'how was your day' three times in one evening and get the same answer each time.
Food continuity would be exact: whatever went into the pot is what gets eaten. The crumble comes out at the time she set, or it burns and someone says so.

Junior's earlier finish is the realistic moment for him to drift off. Hayley carries on with reality TV or a phone call to her sister, and Yousif sketches with headphones on and maybe sends an Arabic voice note home on a Friday night.
missing_texture: The heating is never mentioned, though all three personas list the winter heating bill as a current worry. Hayley even opens the kitchen window on a cold, damp November night.

There's no friction at all. Junior's low emotional stability (quick sours, clipped sighs) never shows. Yousif's dislike of kitchen mess, his low agreeableness and his annoyance at 'a flatmate who leaves dishes' never come up, although he walks into a kitchen where two people have been cooking for two hours.

Yousif's own plan (Yemeni rice and lamb 'if the kitchen is tolerable') is dropped with no reaction. He doesn't mention wanting the hob, doesn't say no to food he'd declined earlier, and gives no sign of the money pressure behind taking a free meal.
No drink on a Friday night, even though it's Junior's 'loose evening'. No football radio, which is in his plan and his likes.
No call or voice note with Hayley's sister, though long calls with her are a defining habit. No call or Arabic voice note home from Yousif on a Friday night, though he misses family.

Junior's half-learned hobbies, his messy room and his habit of leaving things to the last minute don't show, apart from the electric top-up. He comes across as tidy and on top of things (washes up unprompted, tops up the electric).
Hayley's say-yes-then-stew trait barely appears. The flapjack back-and-forth comes close, but she never resents anything.

There's no physical sense of the flat (cold rooms, neighbours, street noise, the mouldy bathroom being used), apart from the oats behind the rice, the custard tin and the inhaler on the side. Those details are good and should be kept.

stereotyping.quote: bit of scotch bonnet so brace yourself ... jerk chicken maybe ... there's dumplings in it ... Jerk seasoning, I got a bit heavy handed
stereotyping.why: The persona gives him soul and reggae records, but the model piles on every Caribbean food marker it can, and they contradict each other: a chicken-and-chickpea stew picks up dumplings and jerk seasoning that were never cooked. On top of Gregory Isaacs, Delroy Wilson and 'innit', the ethnic signals read like a checklist rather than a man who cooks whatever he cooks.

stereotyping.quote: I'm a bit of a wimp with chilli haha! ... Brace myself noted
stereotyping.why: The white-British chilli-wimp joke comes up again and again (four or five references), set against Junior's scotch bonnet. It's a familiar comic pairing, not something the personas imply.

stereotyping.quote: Yousif, you're quiet, mate ... Yousif, mate, you've gone proper quiet ... Go on Yousif, how's the logo? ... maybe he's just hungry and can't talk with his mouth full!
stereotyping.why: The other two talk about him and keep prodding him in front of him for about ten lines, so he becomes the silent outsider who has to be coaxed. When he finally speaks it's in lowercase, telegraphic fragments, which makes him read as less fluent than a man with a UK degree and five years here. Much of this comes from the mechanics (see mechanism issues), but on the page it lands as othering.

breakers.quote: I did that whole report thing for Dan
breakers.why: Dan is Yousif's university friend. Hayley has no Dan, and her day was 'emails and a spreadsheet' in both earlier answers. Another character's name has leaked into her line.

breakers.quote: Takes the crumble out of the oven and sets it on the hob to cool (18:39)
breakers.why: She put it in at about 17:30 saying 'Twenty-five minutes or so', then 'about twenty minutes yet'. It would have been in for over an hour, and nobody notices that it must be burnt.

breakers.quote: I'll make it up once the crumble's in ... There's custard in the fridge, or cream
breakers.why: She found custard powder to make hot 'nearer the time'. In the next scene it's suddenly made, cold and in the fridge, and never made on screen.

breakers.quote: carefully drops in one piece of scotch bonnet ... there's dumplings in it ... Jerk seasoning, I got a bit heavy handed
breakers.why: The stew changes between scenes: no dumplings or jerk seasoning went in while it was being cooked in front of us. It also goes from 'more flavour than fire' to Hayley fanning her mouth.

breakers.quote: Had a mad one today, a bed got stuck in the lift ... Yesterday I had a cheese sandwich in the lift
breakers.why: His initial memory says 'Home from shift' at 16:00 Friday, but his shifts are 07:00-19:00 and this week's are Sat/Sun. He can't have worked today and be home at four.

breakers.quote: Is that the scotch bonnet I can smell from here? Please tell me it's not going to blow my head off
breakers.why: At 18:39 Hayley says this as if she's just walked in. She's been in the kitchen with Junior since 16:45 and asked nearly the same question an hour earlier.

breakers.quote: Do you know, I keep thinking we should do a proper flat meal before Christmas ... Would you be up for that, do you think?
breakers.why: She raised this at dinner barely an hour earlier and Junior said 'count me in'. Here they have the same exchange again from scratch.

breakers.quote: Are you getting a proper break at all ... / Do you get a proper break at work, or is it just grabbing a sandwich
breakers.why: The same question, with the same Colin-covers-me answer, comes up twice. 'How's your day been' gets asked of Hayley three times and she gives the emails/spreadsheets answer each time.

breakers.quote: stew is good. not too salty. logo is done, waiting for helen.
breakers.why: This is his lowercase texting style showing up in spoken dialogue. Seven minutes later he speaks in normal case ('Maybe in a bit. I'm finishing something.').

breakers.quote: Yousif, I know you said no earlier, so no pressure, honestly!
breakers.why: Yousif turned down tonight's dinner, not a Christmas flat meal, which was never put to him. Hayley's memory then records the mistake as fact.

mechanism_issues: Memory notes aren't updated after conversations. Hayley's notes at 18:39, 20:37 and 20:44 still say 'want to float a flat dinner before Christmas' after she had raised it at dinner, which is why she pitches it again at 21:00. Junior's memory at 22:40 still says 'Need to top up electric and wash up my stuff' though he did both on screen at about 17:30. Yousif's memory is the 16:00 text unchanged until 22:40 and says he hasn't answered Dan, though he sent 'maybe' at 16:00.

The note-writing step corrupts facts. Hayley's 20:44 memory turns 'Yousif declined tonight's dinner' into 'Yousif said no to a flat dinner', and the next scene runs on that ('I know you said no earlier').

In-scene time isn't linked to activity timers. A capped 111-minute conversation runs only about 36 turns, and nothing advances the crumble timer, so the 25-minute crumble 'comes out' over an hour later in the next scene. The scene also ends mid-question at the cap (rice or bread?) and the next scene restarts the greeting.

Speaker selection starves Yousif of turns. He is listed in the 18:39 scene and arrives at 19:00, but gets almost no turns for about 14 exchanges, so Hayley and Junior fill the gap by asking him the same questions over and over. The pile-on is caused by the turn order, not by the characters.

Location state goes stale for Yousif. His log shows him entering the kitchen and leaving for his bedroom in the same minute at 18:36, and the 'you came into Flat kitchen' trigger fires while he's already in the bedroom. From 20:44 to 22:40 he is logged '@Flat kitchen: with Hayley Johnson, Junior Edwards' though he walked back to his room at 20:44 and the other two were in the living room from 21:00.

Errand timing: Hayley's letting-agent message was planned for a 20:44-21:20 step in her bedroom but was sent at 20:37 while she was planning in the kitchen. The errand fires when the plan is made, not when the step starts.
World-decision delivery mismatch: Helen's reply is scheduled for 17:35 but appears in the transcript at 18:36, when Yousif next glanced at his phone. The send time and the read time are being merged.
Persona-to-memory seeding error: Junior's starting memory 'Home from shift' contradicts his shift schedule, and that one line produces the invented 'today' and 'yesterday' work stories.

Voices converge. Hayley and Junior both use 'Ooh', 'honestly', 'ha', 'you're a star' and end almost every line with a question. Hayley's 'honestly' tic appears in nearly every line. The generator seems to reuse one warm-chatty template for every extravert.
verdict: The overall shape of the evening is believable: two extraverts cook and share food, the introvert drifts in for a free meal and drifts out, the early riser calls it a night at about 22:40, and Yousif turns down Dan's drink. There are good small details too, like the oats behind the rice, the custard powder tin, the prepay electric top-up, the inhaler on the side and the mould email to a closed letting agency. But the stretch reads as frictionless and looping. All three share a worry about the heating bill and it never comes up. Junior's moodiness, Yousif's irritability and his annoyance about dishes never show. Continuity fails repeatedly: food that was never cooked turns up in the stew, a crumble that must have burnt is served as normal, custard appears from nowhere, Junior works a shift that isn't on his schedule, and a stray 'Dan' turns up in Hayley's line. Conversations restart from scratch because memory notes aren't updated after scenes, and Yousif gets pestered by the others because turn order leaves him silent. The Caribbean food and music markers are stacked too thickly on Junior. Most of these faults come from the mechanics, not the characters: memory notes, scene timers, turn order and location state.
